title: Layered Enterprise Audit Gate SOP - Internal Operational Distillation
provenance: Host-provided layered audit model plus recurring review failures observed in local development sessions. Patterns only: no project names, no conversation excerpts, no filesystem paths.

claims.text: High-risk engineering work benefits from explicit layer coverage: requirements, architecture, data model, interface contract, implementation, testing, operations/observability, security, migration/rollback, and acceptance.
A generic implementation review prompt often misses upstream and downstream failures such as requirements drift, schema safety, API compatibility, observability, rollback, and acceptance evidence.
The layer model should stay a host-agent scheduling prior. Turning it into a mandatory committee for every change increases ceremony and cost without improving evidence quality on small fixes.
Redlines should be union-merged and verified first-hand by the host; majority vote should never drop a cited blocker.

hypotheses.text: Layer-assigned heterogeneous auditors find more HIGH/CRITICAL blockers on high-risk changes than a single generic implementation audit prompt.
A scope matrix with explicit layer exemptions lowers unnecessary audit cost on small fixes without hiding redlines on high-risk changes.

anti_patterns.name: ceremonial-all-layers
anti_patterns.description: Running all ten layers on tiny changes without scope triage or exemptions.

anti_patterns.name: committee-as-router
anti_patterns.description: Letting the audit path choose the workflow instead of the host agent.

anti_patterns.name: vote-away-redlines
anti_patterns.description: Using majority agreement to drop a cited blocker.

anti_patterns.name: exit-code-acceptance
anti_patterns.description: Treating exit code 0 as acceptance without reading artifacts and contracts first-hand.
